claims.text: In equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi, the combination of deformation behavior, hardness, and strength is governed by formation of a stable solid-solution phase.
The formation or stability of the solid-solution phase is influenced by alloy composition.
The formation or stability of the solid-solution phase is influenced by processing history.
The starting equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi alloy is in a simple solid-solution state.
A stable solid-solution phase enhances plasticity in CoCrFeNiTi.
A stable solid-solution phase enhances machinability in CoCrFeNiTi.
The absence of precipitation hardening or other strengthening mechanisms lowers the hardness of the solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi alloy.
The absence of precipitation hardening or other strengthening mechanisms lowers the strength of the solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi alloy.
The starting alloy will have favorable plasticity relative to other high-entropy alloys.
The starting alloy will have favorable machinability relative to other high-entropy alloys.
The starting alloy will have relatively low hardness compared with other high-entropy alloys.
The starting alloy will have relatively low strength compared with other high-entropy alloys.
The hypothesis is intended to apply from 25 °C to 600 °C under uniaxial tensile loading.
